akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ﴾: among the Arabs are those who say "أنتَ حِلٌّ" and "أنتَ حَلال" ("you are out of the state of consecration"), "أَنْتَ حِرْمٌ" and "أَنتَ حَرامٌ" ("you are in the state of consecration"), and "هو المُحِلّ" and "المُحْرِم". [And] you say "أَحْلَلْنا" and "أحْرَمْنا", and you say "حَلَلْنا", which is the good (form).

akhfash:11-11.t: And He said ﴿فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ﴾: He means ﴿فَلَمْ يَقَتْحِمْ﴾ ("he did not attempt"), as He said ﴿فَلاَ صَدَّقَ﴾, that is: he did not believe (فلم يُصَدِّقْ).

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾, that is: "the steep path is the freeing of a neck ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ﴾" (العقبةُ فكُّ رقبةٍ). And some read ﴿فَكَّ رقبةً﴾, and that is not as good; ﴿فكُّ رقبةٍ﴾ is the good (reading).

akhfash:14-15.t: And He said ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾ ﴿يَتِيماً﴾: "اليتيم" (the orphan) is accusative through "الإِطعام" (the maṣdar, "feeding").

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ﴾: لا is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِهذَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْبَلَدِ﴾: badal (substitute); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is parenthetical and has no grammatical position; ﴿بِهذَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿الْبَلَدِ﴾: badal (substitute) for the demonstrative.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَوالِدٍ﴾: conjoined to البلد; ﴿وَما﴾: also conjoined to البلد; ﴿وَلَدَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾: the hamza is a particle of reproachful interrogation, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened from the heavy (anna), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَنْ يَقْدِرَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾: agent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يَقُولُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَهْلَكْتُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿مالًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لُبَداً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾: the hamza is a particle of reproachful interrogation, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened from the heavy (anna), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَمْ يَرَهُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾: agent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ﴾: the hamza is a particle of affirmative interrogation, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿عَيْنَيْنِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَلِساناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: its second object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فَلَا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and لا is negative; ﴿اقْتَحَمَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْعَقَبَةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مَا الْعَقَبَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فَكُّ﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿رَقَبَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is explicative.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿إِطْعامٌ﴾: conjoined to فك; ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿ذِي﴾: naʿt (adjective) of يوم; ﴿مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿يَتِيماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of إطعام; ﴿ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of يتيما, muḍāf to مقربة.

daas-irab:16-16.t: Conjoined to the preceding verse, and its i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَتَواصَوْا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿بِالصَّبْرِ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and the relative noun is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿هُمْ أَصْحابُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين; ﴿الْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause الذين… is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿نارٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنتَ حِلٌّ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ﴾.
He says: it is lawful for you; He made it lawful on the day of the conquest of Mecca. It was not lawful before it and will not be lawful after it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ﴾.
He swore by Adam and his offspring. (ما) is acceptable for people; similar to it is: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالأُنْثَى﴾ — and He is the creator of the male and the female — and similar to it: ﴿فَانكِحُوا مَا طابَ لَكُم مِن النِّسَاءِ﴾, and He did not say: من طاب.
Likewise: ﴿ولا تَنْكِحُوا مَا نَكَحَ آباؤُكُمْ مِن النِّساءِ﴾. All of this is permissible in Arabic. (ما) together with what follows it may also be in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), as in His saying: ﴿والسَّماءِ وَمَا بَنَاهَا﴾, ﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا﴾, as though He said: by the sky and its building, and a soul and its fashioning; and a father and his begetting; and His creating the male and the female. Whichever way you take it, it is correct.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ﴾.
He says: upright and erect. It is also said: created in toil (كبد) — he was created to labour and struggle with the affair of this world and the affair of the Hereafter. [138/a] It was revealed about a man of Banū Jumaḥ who was given the kunya Abū al-Ashaddayn. He used to put the ʿUkāẓ leather under his feet, then order ten men to pull it from under his feet, and the leather would tear while his feet did not move. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾ (5) — because of his strength — ﴿أَن لَّن يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ﴾ (5), while Allah has power over him. Then He said: he says: "I have spent much wealth in enmity to Muhammad ﷺ", and he is lying. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ (7) in his spending.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالاً لُّبَداً﴾.
اللبد: much. Some said its singular is لُبدة and لُبَد is a plural. Some took it as a singular on the pattern of قُثَم and حُطَم; in both interpretations it means much. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read: "مالاً لُبَّداً", with shadda, like رُكَّع; as though he meant: مالٌ لابدٌ, and مالان لابدان, and أموالٌ لُبَّد. الأموال and المال may have one meaning.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ﴾.
The two highways (النجدان): the way of good and the way of evil.
He said: [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: [al-Kisāʾī narrated to me, saying: Qays narrated to me] and Qays narrated to me from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqa from Abū ʿUmāra from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلنَّجْدَينِ﴾. He said: good and evil.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ ٱقتَحَمَ ٱلْعَقَبَةَ﴾.
No other clause containing (لا) was joined to His saying [فلا اقتحم], although the Arabs hardly ever use (لا) singly in speech without repeating it in another clause, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صَلَّى﴾ and ﴿لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾. [That is] because it is one of those whose meaning is at its end, so one sufficed for another. Do you not see that He explained the scaling of the steep pass by two things, saying: ﴿فَكّ رَقبةً، أو أطعم فى يومٍ ذى مسغبة﴾, then ﴿ثم كان [من الذين آمنوا]﴾, so He explained it by three things? So it is as though at the beginning of the speech it was: he did neither this, nor this, nor this.
The general public read: ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبةٍ (13) أو إِطعامٌ﴾ (14), and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read: "فَكَّ رقبةً", and so did ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Marwazī narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from ʿAlī that he read it: "فَكَّ رقبةً أو أطعمَ". That is the closer of the two to correct Arabic, because الإطعام is a noun, and a noun should be coordinated with a noun like it; so if it were said: ثم إن كان أشكلُ للإطعام والفك [Translator's note: the sentence is garbled in the source; the sense is: «ثم كان» (a verb) matches the verbal forms better than the nouns الإطعام and الفك]. So we chose: فكَّ رقبةً, because of His saying: "ثم كان". The other interpretation is permissible: you imply (أن) in it and drop it [138/b], so it becomes [«فكيون» in the source, read «فيكون»] like the poet's saying:
ألا أيهاذا الزَّاجِرى أحْضُرَ الْوغى * وأَنْ أَشْهَدَ اللَّذَّاتِ هل أنتَ مُخْلِدِى
(O you who chide me for attending battle and for partaking in pleasures — can you make me live forever?)
Do you not [«ألاى» in the source] see that the appearance of (أن) at the end of the speech indicates that it is coordinated with another like it at the beginning of the speech, which he dropped?

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾.
[A day] of famine. If it were "ذا مسغبة", you would make it an attribute of the orphan, as though He said: or feeding, on a day, an orphan who is in hunger, or a poor man. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās that he passed by a poor man clinging to the dust out of need, and said: This is the one of whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ﴾ (16). ﴿والموصَدة﴾ (20): it is read with hamza and without hamza, and it means: closed over.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Balad
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ﴾: by "the town" here Mecca is meant. The meaning is: ”أُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ“ ("I swear by this town"), and ”لا“ was inserted for emphasis (tawkīd), just as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29] ("so that the People of the Book may know"). It was also read: ”لَأُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ“, in which case the lām is the lām of the oath and of emphasis. This reading is rare, and it is far-fetched in Arabic, because the lām of the oath does not enter a future-tense verb unless the nūn [of emphasis] is with it: you say ”لَأضْرِبَنَّ زَيْدًا“ ("I will surely strike Zayd"), and ”لَأضْرِبُ“ is not permitted when you mean the present. And Sībawayh and al-Khalīl claimed that this lām enters together with ”إنَّ“, and so it is made sufficient in the chapter of ”إنَّ“: you say ”إنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ“ ("I surely love you").

zajjaj:2-2.t: And the meaning of ﴿وَأنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَذا البَلَدِ﴾ ("and you are free [of restriction] in this town"): Mecca was made lawful for the Prophet, peace be upon him, for an hour of the day, and it was not lawful for anyone before him nor for anyone after him. And the meaning of ”أُحِلَّتْ لَهُ“ ("it was made lawful for him") is: its game was made lawful for him, and that its fresh herbage be cut and its trees be lopped. One says: ”رَجُلٌ حِلٌّ“, ”حَلالٌ“ and ”مُحَلٌّ“ (a man in the non-sacral state); and likewise ”رَجُلٌ حَرامٌ“, ”حِرْمٌ“ and ”مُحْرِمٌ“ (a man in the sacral state).

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿وَوالِدٍ وما ولَدَ﴾ ("and by a begetter and what he begot"): it has come in the exegesis that its meaning is Adam and his offspring; and its meaning has also come as: every begetter and every one begotten.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في كَبَدٍ﴾: this is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). The meaning is: "I swear by these things: We have certainly created the human being in kabad", that is, he endures hardship (yukābidu) in his affairs in this world and the Hereafter. And it was said: ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾ means he was created upright, walking on his two legs, while all other things and animals are not upright. And it was said ﴿فِي كَبَدٍ﴾: the human being was created in his mother's womb with his head toward her head, and when she wishes to give birth the head turns downward.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿أنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أحَدٌ﴾ ("that no one has power over him"): this, it has come in the exegesis, is a man who was extremely strong. An ʿUkāẓī hide used to be spread out for him, and he would stand on it and it would be torn apart, so that nothing came out from under his feet except in pieces, because of his strength. He was called Kalada. So it was said: "Does he think, because of his strength, that no one has power over him, and that he will not be resurrected?!" And it was said: "[Does he think] that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has no power over him?" — because he did not believe in the Resurrection.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿يَقُولُ أهْلَكْتُ مالا لُبَدًا﴾ ("he says: I have squandered heaps of wealth"). It was read: ”أهْلَكْتُ مالًا لُبَدًا“, and it is also read: ”لُبَّدًا“. The meaning of ”لُبَدًا“ is "much", part of it matted (lubbida) onto part. The pattern ”فُعَلٌ“ is for abundance: one says ”رَجُلٌ حُطَمٌ“ when a man smashes (ḥaṭm) a great deal. And whoever reads ”لُبَّدًا“, it is the plural of ”لابِدٌ“.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿أيَحْسَبُ أنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أحَدٌ﴾ ("does he think that no one saw him?"): that is, does he think that what he spent is not counted against him? And in the discourse there is evidence that he claimed he had spent a great deal which did not benefit him.

zajjaj:8-9.t: And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ألَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ﴾ ﴿وَلِسانًا وشَفَتَيْنِ﴾ ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾ [al-Balad: 10] ("Have We not made for him two eyes, and a tongue and two lips, and guided him to the two highways?"): that is, have We not done for him that by which one infers that Allah is able to resurrect him and to count against him what he does?!

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: the two clear ways. ”اَلنَّجْدُ“ is raised ground. So the meaning is: "Have We not made known to him the way of good and the way of evil, as clear as the clarity of two elevated roads?!"

zajjaj:11-11.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ﴾: the meaning is ”فَلَمْ يَقْتَحِمِ العَقَبَةَ“ ("but he did not attempt the steep ascent").
Just as He said: ﴿فَلا صَدَّقَ ولا صَلّى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 31] ("for he neither affirmed nor prayed"). Here He mentioned ”لا“ only once, whereas the Arabs rarely speak in such a position without ”لا“ twice or more; you would hardly say ”لا حَيَّيْتَنِي“ meaning ”ما حَيَّيْتَنِي“ ("you did not greet me"), but if you said "[لا] حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي" ("you neither greeted me nor visited me") it would be sound. [Translator's note: the source reads «حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي» without the first «لا»; the argument requires «لا حَيَّيْتَنِي ولا زُرْتَنِي».] The meaning [of the repeated lā] in ﴿فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ﴾ is present: a second ”لا“ is as if it were in the discourse, because His saying ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [al-Balad: 17] ("then he was of those who believed") points to the meaning ”فَلا اقْتَحَمَ العَقَبَةَ ولا آمَنَ“ ("he neither attempted the steep ascent nor believed").

zajjaj:13-14.t: It was read: ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾ ﴿أوْ إطْعامٌ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾ ("the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of hunger"), and it was read: ”فَكَّ رَقَبَةً أوْ أطْعَمَ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ“ ("he freed a slave or fed on a day of hunger"), and both are permissible. Whoever said ﴿فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ﴾, the meaning is: "attempting the steep ascent is the freeing of a slave or feeding"; and whoever read ”فَكَّ رَقَبَةً“, it is construed according to the sense. And ”اَلْمَسْغَبَةُ“ is famine.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying: ﴿يَتِيمًا ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ﴾: its meaning is "possessed of kinship". You say: ”زَيْدٌ ذُو قَرابَتِي، وذُو مَقْرَبَتِي“ ("Zayd is one of my kin"), whereas ”زَيْدٌ قَرابَتِي“ is ugly, because ”اَلْقَرابَةُ“ is the maṣdar (verbal noun). The poet said:
يَبْكِي عَلَيْهِ غَرِيبٌ لَيْسَ يَعْرِفُهُ ∗∗∗ وذُو قَرابَتِهِ في الحَيِّ مَسْرُورُ
(A stranger who does not know him weeps over him, while his kinsman in the tribe is glad.)
And His saying: ﴿ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ﴾ [al-Balad: 16]: He means that, from his poverty, he has cleaved to the dust.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its meaning is: "When he did that, and had bound himself to faith, and then remained steadfast upon his faith." ﴿وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ ("and enjoined one another to patience"): that is, upon obedience to Allah, and patience in refraining from entering into acts of disobedience to Him. Then, along with that, he was of those who enjoin one another to compassion; those are the people of good fortune (al-yumn) for themselves, that is, they were bringers of blessing upon themselves, not of ill omen.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا هم أصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ﴾: that is, they are the bringers of ill omen upon themselves. We seek refuge in Allah from the Fire.

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ نارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ ("over them is a Fire closed in"): it is also read without hamza; its meaning is "closed over". One says ”آصَدْتُ البابَ“ and ”أوْصَدْتُهُ“ ("I closed the door") when I have shut it.
